questions.q: What does a CloudWatch Alarm actually do?
options: Watches a single metric continuously and triggers automatically when it crosses a defined threshold
Automatically fixes any resource that is performing poorly
Only works for metrics in the AWS/S3 namespace
Replaces the need for any metric data entirely
questions.explain: An alarm removes the need for a human to watch a dashboard — it fires the moment the metric it's watching crosses the threshold you've set.

questions.q: To express "CPUUtilization above 80% for 5 minutes" as an alarm, which pieces do you need?
options: A period (e.g. 300 seconds), a comparison operator (GreaterThanThreshold), and a threshold (80)
Only the metric name — AWS infers the rest automatically
A VPC route table entry pointing at the metric
An IAM policy with no other configuration
questions.explain: An alarm's definition combines the metric, statistic, period, comparison operator, and threshold — period 300 with one evaluation period expresses "for 5 minutes."

questions.q: What does the INSUFFICIENT_DATA alarm state mean?
options: CloudWatch hasn't yet received enough data points to judge whether the alarm should be OK or ALARM
The alarm has permanently failed and must be recreated
The metric has definitely breached its threshold
The SNS topic attached to the alarm has been deleted
questions.explain: INSUFFICIENT_DATA is normal, for example right after an instance first launches, before enough data points exist.

questions.q: What is the real mechanism an alarm uses to send a notification, such as an email or text message?
options: The alarm publishes to an SNS (Simple Notification Service) topic, which fans the message out to its subscribers
The alarm sends the email directly from CloudWatch's own mail server
CloudTrail delivers the notification on CloudWatch's behalf
Notifications are sent only through the AWS Management Console UI
questions.explain: An alarm's --alarm-actions points at an SNS topic ARN; SNS is what actually fans the notification out to email, SMS, or webhook subscribers.

questions.q: A new email subscription was just added to an SNS topic used by an alarm. The alarm has already fired. Why might the subscriber have received nothing?
options: The subscription is still "pending confirmation" until the subscriber clicks the confirmation link AWS sent them
SNS only supports SMS, not email, as a protocol
The alarm must be in the OK state for notifications to send
Email subscriptions expire after one use
questions.explain: A brand-new subscription sits pending confirmation until it's confirmed — until then, the alarm can fire and the notification simply goes nowhere.
